note: A screen, not an audit: questions worth asking and the data needed to answer them. No savings are computed; typical benefits are the cited sources' general wording.

questions.question: If this historical example applies to a receiving installation, what current approved evidence distinguishes high-level indication/notification from automatic action on incoming unloading?

evidence.text: equipment HYPO_BULK reads "HYPO_BULK Sodium hypochlorite bulk tank"

data_requests.item: Receiving scope, applicability and engineering owner
where: site records: company-approved scope and designated controls/document owner
data_requests.how: First decide whether this historical question applies to an identified receiving asset/process and period. No receiving company, owner, due date or current configuration is supplied here; if not applicable, record that reason rather than inventing a collection task.

data_requests.item: Current signal function and incoming-transfer action path
where: site records: approved current control narrative, logic/cause-and-effect revision and signal mapping
data_requests.how: Retain revision/locator and distinguish indication, ordinary feedback, operator notification, automatic protective action and remote commanded action. Identify the affected unloading-to-bulk final element or endpoint; do not infer an installed trip or its absence from a level indicator or a missing model record.

questions.decision_rule: Historical reading is already answered: the report describes high-level notification, without automatic incoming-transfer shutdown (p.23 section5.2). Close that bounded historical question with its citation. Only an explicitly applicable current-installation question needs receiving records and owner review; record unknowns or not-applicable rather than prescribing equipment or settings.

typical_benefit.wording: No operational benefit or measured usefulness is established. The source supports a distinction between notification and endpoint-specific action.
source_titles: MGPI: CSB, Key Lessons from the MGPI Processing Inc. Toxic Chemical Release, 2017-01-I-KS, December 2017

questions.limits: Known historical answer to retain: the sodium hypochlorite bulk-tank high-level signal notified operators and was not configured to shut the transfer automatically (p.23 section5.2). The report records alarm activation at7:59AM and says awareness/evacuation was likely about the same time; do not turn likely into exact timing. This source does not establish every ordinary-control use, present-day configuration, required safeguards or operating safety. HYPO_BULK and LI_HYPO are project aliases.

questions.question: If this example applies to a receiving installation, which current approved remote/emergency action actually affects unloading-to-bulk transfer, separately from bulk-to-day-tank or downstream processes?

evidence.text: equipment HYPO_BULK reads "HYPO_BULK Sodium hypochlorite bulk tank"

where: site records: approved P&ID/line tracing and remote-command or emergency-stop functional description
data_requests.how: A receiving engineering owner must identify applicability, process segment, actual final element and current revision. Distinguish incoming unloading-to-bulk from bulk-to-day/downstream transfer; action on one segment does not establish action on another.

data_requests.item: Evidence for any asserted current capability
where: site records: applicable approved functional-test/acceptance record or other owner-approved action-path evidence
data_requests.how: Retain declared test scope, revision/date, result and unresolved discrepancies. No present-day test, acceptance or operational action is supplied here; no new test or live action is instructed.

questions.decision_rule: The bounded report-era answer is already sufficient: downstream emergency/remote action existed, but incoming unloading lacked remote shutdown (p.23 section5.2; transfer segments pp.7-8 section2.3). Retain that answer. A separately accepted current-installation claim needs endpoint-specific receiving evidence and a reviewer, not inference from the drawing or the historical source.

typical_benefit.wording: No operational benefit or measured usefulness is established. The source supports a distinction between notification and endpoint-specific action.
source_titles: MGPI: CSB, Key Lessons from the MGPI Processing Inc. Toxic Chemical Release, 2017-01-I-KS, December 2017

questions.limits: Known historical answer to retain: two emergency-stop buttons and control-system remote actions affected downstream equipment; one could stop bulk-to-day flow but not unloading-to-bulk flow. The report says even activation would not mitigate the reaction because unloading lacked remote shutdown (p.23 section5.2). The manually activated unloading-area deluge addressed cloud suppression, not automatic unloading isolation. No current action capability/absence, named owner or engineering prescription follows.
